caption:
He plays violin for the LA Philharmonic. He also plays it inside homeless shelters and jails.

Vijay Gupta, an Indian-American violinist, joined the Los Angeles Philharmonic in 2007 at age 19. In 2011, while still a full-time orchestra violinist, he founded Street Symphony - bringing live classical music and teaching artistry directly into LA's homeless shelters, clinics, county jails and state hospitals. Street Symphony has since presented thousands of performances and lessons for some of LA's most marginalized communities, work that later earned Gupta a 2018 MacArthur Fellowship.

Classical music is usually kept behind concert-hall doors. He decided the people who needed it most should never have to knock.

Sources: LA Phil, NEA (2007-2026)
